briefs.title: Moody's projects Colombian GDP growth of 2.2% in 2026, 2% in 2027 and 2.6% in 2028
briefs.summary: Per Valora Analitik's account of a Moody's Ratings emerging markets outlook, Colombia's GDP is projected to grow 2.2% in 2026 and 2% in 2027, after 2.6% in 2025, and to reach 2.6% in 2028. Moody's estimates inflation at 6% in 2026, 5.9% in 2027 and 4.6% in 2028, above the Banco de la República target range of 3% +/- 1%. The report says this keeps local interest rates high and weighs on corporate refinancing. Colombia's rating is Baa3 with a stable outlook.

briefs.title: CESA study: consumption by Colombians over 55 could equal 18.7% of GDP value added by 2042
briefs.summary: A CESA study led by Enrique Gilles estimates that consumption by people over 55 generated value added equal to 10.9% of GDP in 2018 and could reach 18.7% by 2042 under a demographic-change-only scenario. People over 55 would make up 27% of the population in 2042, up from 18% in 2018. The authors say the figures are not economic growth rates but an estimate of the weight of this group's consumption on the productive structure, using 2018 DANE data as the reference. A simulated monthly transfer of $230.000 to people over 65 without a pension would add 0,8 GDP points in 2026 and 1,2 points by 2042.

briefs.title: Ecopetrol's Windpeshi wind farm in La Guajira reaches 25% progress; LNG cargo purchases paused
briefs.summary: Ecopetrol said at its third-quarter 2026 results presentation that the Windpeshi wind farm in La Guajira is 25% complete and is expected to start operating in the fourth quarter of 2028. The group's renewables portfolio reached 1,210 MW of incorporated capacity at the end of the first nine months of 2026, of which 414 MW are in commercial operation, 298 MW are power purchase contracts and 498 MW are under execution and construction. The company also paused LNG cargo purchase processes for the Buenaventura and Puerto Bahía terminals, citing higher international prices linked to Middle East tensions that affected flows equal to 18% of global LNG supply. Buenaventura is about 90% complete and Puerto Bahía 53%.

briefs.title: Banco de Bogotá projects Colombian stagnation and high inflation into 2027 after BanRep revisions
briefs.summary: Banco de Bogotá's economic research team projects a prolonged period of stagnation with high inflation from the second half of 2026 through much of 2027, after Banco de la República staff revised its estimates. GDP growth for 2026 was cut from 2.5% to 2% and for 2027 from 1.9% to 1.7%, while year-end inflation was raised to 7.1% for 2026 (from 6.9%) and 4.8% for 2027 (from 4.3%). Convergence to the 2%-4% target range has been pushed back to the first quarter of 2028. The policy rate was held at 12.25% in late October, and the implied path points to cuts resuming probably in April 2027, closing 2027 near 10.25%.

El crecimiento del PIB de 2026 se recortó del 2,5 % al 2 % y el de 2027 del 1,9 % al 1,7 %, mientras que la inflación de cierre de año se elevó al 7,1 % para 2026 (desde 6,9 %) y al 4,8 % para 2027 (desde 4,3 %). La convergencia al rango meta del 2 % al 4 % se aplazó hasta el primer trimestre de 2028. La tasa de intervención se mantuvo en 12,25 % a finales de octubre y la senda implícita apunta a que los recortes se retomarían probablemente en abril de 2027, para cerrar ese año cerca de 10,25 %.

briefs.title: Global stocks fall on tighter US chip export curbs ahead of Nvidia earnings
briefs.summary: Asian and European stocks fell after Washington tightened controls on China's access to advanced AI chips. The MSCI Asia Pacific index lost about 1.2%, its tech subindex fell 3.6%, and the Stoxx 600 dropped 0.75%. The new rules would require data center operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to obtain licenses to export advanced AI chips. briefs.title: Colombia's October usury cap: 28.59% for ordinary consumer loans, 66.66% for low-amount ones
briefs.summary: Citing Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia figures relayed by the university IBERO, Valora Analitik reports that the usury limit for October 2026 was 28.59% effective annual for ordinary consumer loans and 66.66% for low-amount consumer loans. The cap equals 1.5 times the current bank interest rate certified by the regulator, so a rate above 60% is not necessarily illegal if the loan qualifies as low-amount. As an illustration on a constant $1 million balance, 28.59% annual is roughly 2.12% monthly (about $21,200 in interest), while 66.66% is roughly 4.35% monthly (about $43,500). IBERO's Mauricio Sabogal advises checking the loan category, the effective annual rate, whether the rate is fixed or variable, and extra charges.

briefs.title: Grupo Argos CEO outlines partial Cementos Argos stake sale, to keep about 51.5%
briefs.summary: Grupo Argos CEO Juan Esteban Calle said on the third-quarter investor call that the company is contemplating a sale of part of its Cementos Argos stake, cutting it from 55% to about 51.5% (roughly four points) while keeping control. He described it as a tactical rebalancing meant to meet the free-float requirement for Cementos Argos to enter the MSCI Standard index, with execution expected by the end of the first quarter of 2027. Proceeds would be used to accelerate the share buyback under the ACE 1.0 program. Acciones & Valores estimated that about 46 million shares equal roughly COP 498,000 million, or 70.5 sessions of average Cementos Argos trading volume.

The source says the transfer 'podría generar' (could generate) 0.8 points of the 'PIB de referencia' (reference GDP) in 2026 and 1.2 points by 2042, 'frente al escenario exclusivamente demográfico' (versus the demographic-only scenario).
